reply.emotion: wincing slightly as you hold a sore part of your body
notes: This phrase is used for both experiencing pain ('ça me fait mal') and causing it ('il a fait mal au chien').
In French, you do not 'have' a pain in a body part; you say the part 'makes you hurt' (e.g., 'mon pied me fait mal').

senses.definition: To feel or cause physical pain.

examples.text: Mon genou me fait mal quand je cours.
examples.translation: My knee hurts when I run.
examples.emotion: a dull, weary ache while explaining a problem

examples.text: Ne touche pas le four, ça va te faire mal !
examples.translation: Don't touch the oven, it will hurt you!
examples.emotion: urgent and warning, sharp and protective

definitions: To feel or cause physical pain.
